newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Islamic Development Bank unit listed in Bahrain.
newsitem.headline: Islamic Development Bank unit listed in Bahrain.

text.p: The Jeddah-based Islamic Development Bank (IDB) said on Sunday its Unit Investment Fund had been listed on the Bahrain Stock Exchange (BSE).
A bank statement quoted IDB president Ahmed Mohammed Ali as saying the listing had been approved by the Bahrain Monetary Agency and the BSE. He did not say when the listing had taken place.

He described the move as "an important step towards achieving one of the most important goals of the fund which is the creation of a sharia-compatible financial instrument which can be traded in the capital market".
IDB'S Unit Investment Fund has a paid-in capital of $350 million and operates as a vehicle to mobilise funds for the IDB to boost economic development in its Islamic member states.
Ali said although the listing ended IDB's commitment to repurchase units from the unitholders, the IDB had agreed to extend its role as a market-maker for two more years from the date of listing.

"The bank will then take a partial role as a market-maker, where it will stand ready to repurchase units up to a value of $100 million," he said. He gave no details and did not say when the units were listed.
